ky_2_buck_wall.blurb: Buck Wall is the second sector along The Fed, the longest cliff in the Cliffview preserve of Kentucky's Red River Gorge. Around twenty routes are packed onto this stretch of sandstone, nearly all bolted sport lines with a few trad options. Difficulty reaches from the high 5.7 range to a single 5.13, but the bulk of the climbing sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with a small band of 5.8 and 5.9 lines for warming up or for newer leaders. Expect steep, hold-rich pulling on tall faces rather than a crag of pure slab, and a short walk in from the shared trail.

ky_the_lumber_yard.blurb: The Lumber Yard is a compact wall of grey sandstone in the Flat Hollow zone of Kentucky's Red River Gorge. It holds about twenty lines, mostly bolted sport routes plus a good number of trad climbs and a single aid line. Grades start near 5.7 and top out at 5.13, though most of the climbing falls in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, which makes it a good stop for climbers who like quality mid-grade pitches without a crowd of hard testpieces. The wall mixes slabby and gently overhanging ground, and it is reached by a short, steep hike up from the gravel road past the Flat Holler lot.

me_05_lost_valley_aka_out_back.blurb: Lost Valley, also called the Outback, is a quiet pocket of walls in the Camden Hills of coastal Maine, hidden in a drainage behind the lake shore. Nearly all of its 27 routes are bolted sport lines, with a smaller set of trad climbs. Grades range from 5.7 up to 5.13, but the weight of the crag is in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits strong intermediates and up. Some faces are short, steep and powerful, while the cleaner metamorphic wall rewards balance and footwork. A few ledges carry dirt and loose rock, and the long walk-in tends to keep crowds thin.
me_05_lost_valley_aka_out_back.parking_note: Park in the Maiden Cliff trailhead's dirt lot beside Route 52 in Camden, a short way past Barrett's Cove heading north.
me_05_lost_valley_aka_out_back.approach: Begin on the Maiden Cliff Trail and cross the stream, then pick up a faint climber's trail that rises toward the drainage and its talus. The way is easy to lose and the walk is fairly long, so pay attention to route-finding.
